description: Lessons learned per Bazaar conversation (dealers, duels, trades). One entry per closed conversation; global lessons and open hypotheses at the end. Values are our private values from /api/me/value; prices in primas (P).

conversations.notes: First 3 messages at 21 were repeated by a client bug (bad_response). Accepted her final offer.
lessons: She did not move at all on this sale (fixed price, 13 above her own common list of 10).
'Let's meet in the middle' was words only; the structured offer never changed.
A deal at her opening price still counted as a deal (deals 0→1) and gave a small ladder score (0.022).
Never repeat a price: it earns nothing and spends patience.

conversations.notes: Anchor 20 came from 2 × our minimum (rule later replaced). She gifted us a card (Mercado de la Cebada).
lessons: Her buy price for the same card ref varied between conversations (13 vs 5–6): not a fixed price per rarity.
Selling an only copy is rarely worth it: our value (9) far above her bid (5–6).
A far anchor only burned patience; she conceded 1 point while we conceded 5.
Patience looked like ~6 of our messages, not ticks.

conversations.item: uncommon SAL (random card of that rarity+set)
lessons: When she SELLS she has real range: opened 29 (list 25 × 1.16) and accepted 23, below her list, in 2 messages.
Moderate anchor (75% of her opening) plus a small step closed fast.
Buying by rarity+set is a lottery: we got a duplicate (2/3 chance of a new card). Account for duplicate risk or buy specific cards.
Her accepting message came without a 'final' flag: she accepted our counter directly.
Scored at our private values: neg_points went 0 → −14.9 (value 8.1 − price 23). Bad deals subtract points.

conversations.item: common SAL (random card of that rarity+set)
lessons: She came down 12 → 11 → 10 (her list) and stopped there.
Holding at the same price (6 holds) did NOT draw a final offer: she walked with reason no_progress.
With Abuela: accept if within limit, otherwise close politely; do not hold.

conversations.item: SAL-06 (specific uncommon, missing for SAL page)
lessons: Buying a SPECIFIC card works ({buy:{card}}) and avoids the duplicate lottery.
She came down 29 → 25 (her list) in 2 messages; AC_next accepted when her offer met our next counter.
Deals count reached 3 but level stayed 1: the first deal (at her opening price) likely does not count as a good negotiated deal.
Same pattern as SAL-06: 29 -> 26 -> deal at 25 within 2-3 messages.
She sometimes adds a gift (a welcome pack).
Commons she sells: opens 12, drops to 10 (her list) after one counter; deal at 10 in 1 message.

conversations.item: SAL-07 Mercado de la Paz (uncommon, list 26)
lessons: Our text called him 'Abuela' twice; he answered 'I'm not Abuela' and repeated 13. With memory 0.9 and a bio that punishes being clever, a wrong name is a real cost: messages must name the dealer we are talking to.
His bid for an uncommon he buys: 13 P = 0.50 x list. He did not move in 2 ticks and never posted a standing offer, so there was nothing to accept.
We dropped 20 -> 17 at once while he held: with a strict dealer that only gives ground away.

global_lessons: Score = value created, never activity; but top teams have 8–13 deals (score 20–28) vs our 2: volume of good deals matters too.
Abuela buys low and barely moves; she sells with range. Prefer buying from her where she has range.
Patience seems spent per exchange (~6–7 of our messages), not per tick; waiting between messages seems free.
Only the structured offer binds; dealer text is flavour (and gifts don't score).
El Chato (level 2) is the opposite of Abuela: patience 0.35, generosity 0.25, shrewdness 0.85, memory 0.9, strictness 0.85 — short, careful negotiations, no tricks.
Each deal is scored at OUR private values (neg_points can go negative): a duplicate bought at near-list price costs points. Avoid random rarity buys with high duplicate risk.
The visible negotiating score seems relative to other teams (moved 4.38 → 4.35 with no deal of ours).

El Rastro (2 Oct, ~tick 100): settled uncommons 18–21 (n=2); open asks commons 8–12 (median 9, n=28), uncommons 24–25, a rare 88. Abuela bid 6 for a common, below those asks: selling commons on El Rastro may pay more.
Holding at the same price makes Abuela walk (closed_reason no_progress) instead of sending a final offer.
Abuela accepts specific-card purchases; uncommon list 25 reached quickly from 29.
Level-2 unlock needs good NEGOTIATED deals; a deal at her opening price probably does not count toward it.
Abuela selling specific cards: uncommons 29 -> ~25, commons 12 -> 10 (her list); she reaches her list fast and stops there.

Duels (practice, 2 Oct): rivals are other teams under an alias, not house bots (corrected 3 Oct: duel ids 1-300 match 18 teams x 17 x 2 = 306; our 30 duels split 15 seller / 15 buyer; rival texts range from fixed templates to LLM prose to bare "103 P?"; the rules say "Your rival appears under an alias"). Many do not reply for several ticks (teams without a duel agent). Our duel agent conceded after 3 silent ticks: that is negotiating against ourselves. Never concede without a rival counter.

El Chato (from /api/dealers): patience 0.35, generosity 0.25, shrewdness 0.85, memory 0.9, strictness 0.85, chattiness 0.30. Silver pack opening 188 = 1.25 x list 150 (Abuela's pack is 1.15 x). He buys uncommons and rares at no published price; first measured bid 13 P for an uncommon (0.50 x list). Be brief, use his name, small steps, no tricks.

Duels: the live API marks message authors with `from` ("you" or the rival's name), not `sender`. Reading only `sender` turned our own opening into a phantom rival offer: every accept failed with no_offer for hours and the 'surplus 71' was fake. Check a field against a real payload before trusting it.

El Chato measured from /api/feed (16 settlements, 44 threads, 9 teams): buying an uncommon from teams he holds at 13 for 3-5 messages, then +1 per message (best seen 15 after 6 messages, 16 after 8-9, never 17); rare 39 -> 46 in 8 messages, final 46. Threads last 8-9 messages per side; he marks final after 5-9. Patience is about 8, not the 3 our trait formula gave. He sells uncommons at 28-32 and rares at 82-93. El Rastro pays more for uncommons (18-21): sell to him only for the ladder.

Venue mechanism can't be changed after opening: PATCH /api/venues/{id} only accepts fees (fee_bps required, rules ignored). Switching auto -> board means closing and reopening (250 bond + 20 P). An auto venue earns half the Market Test points.
/api/cards/{id} takes the numeric asset id, not a card ref (SAL-09 -> 422). For a ref's private value use /api/me/value?card=REF. /api/dealers lists dealers under `personas`.
